{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=mechanisms+for+autonomous+objective+discovery+beyond+convex+scalarization+in+multi-objective+reinforcement+learning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.65109/lngi4831\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Non-Linear Scalarization\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) setup naturally arises in many places where an agent optimizes multiple objectives. We consider the problem of MORL where multiple objectives are combined using a non-linear scalarization. We combine the vector objectives with a concave scalarization function and maximize this scalar objective. To work with the non-linear scalarization, in this paper, we propose a solution using steady-state occupancy measures and long-term average rewards. We show that when the scalarization function is element-wise increasing, the optimal policy for the scalarization is also Pareto optimal. To maximize the scalarized objective, we propose a model-based posterior sampling algorithm. Using a novel Bellman error analysis for infinite horizon MDPs based proof, we show that the proposed algorithm obtains a regret bound of ~O(LKDS√A/T) for K objectives, and L-Lipschitz continous scalarization function for MDP with S states, A actions, and diameter D. Additionally, we propose policy-gradient and actor-critic algorithms for MORL. For the policy gradient actor, we obtain the gradient using chain rule, and we learn different critics for each of the K objectives. Finally, we implement our algorithms on multiple environments including deep-sea treasure, and network scheduling setups to demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can optimize non-linear scalarization of multiple objectives.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65109/lngi4831\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 5, 9]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1007/978-3-7091-2822-0_3\", \"title\": [\"Scalarization in Multi Objective Optimization\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-7091-2822-0_3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1985]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1016/j.neucom.2025.132205\", \"title\": [\"Adaptive scalarization in multi-objective reinforcement learning for enhanced robotic arm control\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org…

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=mechanisms+of+path+dependence+and+divergent+value+evolution+in+reinforcement+learning+agents&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6357078\", \"title\": [\"Anticipatory Reinforcement Learning: From Generative Path-Laws to Distributional Value Functions\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper introduces Anticipatory Reinforcement Learning, a novel framework designed to bridge the gap between non-Markovian decision processes and classical reinforcement learning architectures. In environments characterised by jump-diffusions and structural breaks, traditional state-based methods often fail to capture the essential path-dependent geometry required for accurate foresight. We resolve this by lifting the state space into a signatureaugmented manifold, where the history of the process is embedded as a dynamical coordinate. By utilising a selfconsistent field approach, the agent maintains an anticipated proxy of the future path-law, allowing for a deterministic evaluation of expected returns. This transition from stochastic branching to a single-pass linear evaluation significantly reduces computational complexity and variance. We prove that this framework preserves fundamental contraction properties and ensures stable generalisation even in the presence of heavy-tailed noise. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=formal+models+of+research+agenda+abandonment+in+science+and+autonomous+discovery&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6820898\", \"title\": [\"Formal Guarantees for Trustworthy Autonomous Biological Discovery: A Dual-Process Control Framework\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Generative AI now proposes protein sequences and metabolic pathways faster than laboratories can validate them, yet autonomous biological discovery is stalled by an unaddressed trust deficit: in-silico predictions regularly diverge from in-vitro outcomes, and no formal framework exists to bound this gap. We introduce Verifiable Agentic Biotechnology (VAB), a theoretical framework built on three provable guarantees. First, conformal prediction converts point estimates of biological fitness into finite-sample confidence intervals, guaranteeing coverage of true physical fitness with probability at least 1α irrespective of model misspecification. Second, a dual-process Constrained Markov Decision Process routes designs between fast heuristics and expensive mechanistic verifiers, achieving exact computational savings (C 2-C 1)P(σ 1 ≤ τ) while bounding safety degradation at γP(σ 1 ≤ τ). Third, the in-silico to in-vitro reproducibility gap is formalized as a Wasserstein distribution shift, yielding a Distributionally Robust Optimization bound V * DRBO on wet-lab transferability. Each bound is validated on controlled proxy environments and, in the case of conformal prediction, on real protein sequence data. The framework's parameters-α, τ , and ρ-map directly onto regulatory variables, providing a path from ungoverned sequence generation to auditable biological design.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6820898\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1002/9783527855841.ch14\", \"title\": [\"Materials Agents for Autonomous Research\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/9783527855841.ch14\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 3, 17]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6797083\", \"title\": [\"Employment Latency: A Formal Framework for Autonomous Employment Infrastructure, Discovery Latency Resolution, and Point-of-Offer Compliance Integration\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This…
